rich_narrative.summary: founded in 2011, Bayan serves as a non-sectarian graduate school dedicated to producing <cite id="1">ethical leaders and scholars grounded in the Islamic tradition</cite>. The institution operates at a critical intersection of religious education and professional development, offering <cite id="2">Master's degrees in Islamic Chaplaincy, Education, and Theological Studies</cite>. While the organization maintains a positive reputation, its financial profile presents a notable trade-off for donors. In FY2024, Bayan reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $3,153,900</cite>, reflecting a steady <cite id="4">3-year revenue CAGR of 12.3%</cite>. However, its <cite id="5">program expense ratio of 52.0%</cite> remains below the 75% industry benchmark. This suggests that a significant portion of funding is currently directed toward administrative and growth-related infrastructure rather than direct student services. Despite this, the organization demonstrates <cite id="6">strong financial health with 6.7 months of working capital</cite>, providing a resilient foundation for its specialized academic mission. For Muslim donors, the organization is <cite id="7">verified as zakat-eligible</cite>, specifically serving the asnaf categories of <cite id="8">the poor (fuqara) and the needy (masakin)</cite> through its scholarship and leadership training programs.
